body.en: Three-dimensional geometry and similarity ratios appear at the end of the EST II test, often combined with algebraic reasoning.

value.en: lengths \( k \) : areas \( k^2 \) : volumes \( k^3 \)

body.en: Two similar spheres have radii 3 and 6. Find the ratio of their volumes. \[ \text{Ratio of radii}=1:2,\quad\text{Volume ratio}=1^3:2^3=1:8. \]

Sphere: SA \(=4\pi r^2\), V \(=\tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). Cylinder: SA \(=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh\), V \(=\pi r^2 h\). Cone: SA \(=\pi r^2+\pi rl\), V \(=\tfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). For similar solids with scale factor \(k\): area scales as \(k^2\), volume scales as \(k^3\).

label.en: Worked example — Volume of composite solid

body.en:
A solid consists of a cylinder (radius 4 cm, height 6 cm) with a hemisphere on top. Find the total volume.

Cylinder: \(\pi(16)(6) = 96\pi\). Hemisphere: \(\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot\tfrac{4}{3}\pi(64) = \tfrac{128\pi}{3}\).

Total \(= 96\pi + \tfrac{128\pi}{3} = \dfrac{288\pi+128\pi}{3} = \dfrac{416\pi}{3} \approx 435.6\) cm\(^3\).

question.en: Two similar cones have surface areas in the ratio \(4:9\). If the smaller cone has volume \(16\pi\) cm\(^3\), find the volume of the larger.

solution.en: Area ratio \(= k^2 = 4/9\), so \(k = 2/3\). Volume ratio \(= k^3 = 8/27\). Larger volume \(= 16\pi \times 27/8 = 54\pi\) cm\(^3\).
